notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

PC game sound should pop less. Wine kept only 5 ms of sound ready, so a new
sound that started while the console was busy could run dry; it now keeps
60 ms. Each console picks this up at its first PC game launch after the update.

The Extended keyboard has a new row under the bottom one: Esc, Caps, Ctrl, Alt
and Win. Ctrl and Alt stay held until you press them again, for shortcuts, and
they let go when the keyboard closes or the game ends.

The touch buttons' Hide button can sit at either end of a row, or in any corner
when the buttons run down the sides. Before a game starts, the touch options
are now in their own Touch buttons menu under Controllers, with Where they sit
and Hide button; the pause menu's touch screen has the Hide button choice too.

The console's system log can no longer grow past 200 MB. On one console it had
reached 10 GB. The update trims a log that is already bigger.

On the web page, the Steam list folds away, and when there are more than 10
games a row of letters shows one letter's games at a time; search still looks
through all of them. In Browse all files, protected files can be ticked for
Download and Copy, so a boot file can be read or backed up; they still cannot
be changed.

On the RAM page, a custom test that passed with "Commit if it passes" off now
says "Passed, not saved", and opening it offers Save this setting and restart.
A note under the memory voltages says they are the memory's, and that the
CPU's highest voltage is Max voltage, under CPU Settings.

The PC games report now shows how long the Steam client took to start and the
end of Steam's own logs.

Tested on one console.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
